graders.name: names-the-home-mismatch
graders.evidence:
## What's wrong

Not a stale CLI, and not anything to sync or upgrade. The error even says so: `NOTHING IS OUT OF DATE`.

`bootstrap-home.sh` has to pick a `skill-manager` to run the bootstrap with (`pick_cli`, `.skill-manager/skills/git-issue-workflow/scripts/bootstrap-home.sh:790`). It looks for a build shipped by the checkout, then by the enclosing integration repo, then falls back to whatever `skill-manager` is on `PATH`. In your worktree the first two found nothing, so the only candidate was the `PATH` entry — and that entry is **another checkout's home entrypoint**, `/work/other-repo/.skill-manager/bin/cli/skill-manager`.

A `<home>/bin/cli/skill-manager` shim binds the home it lives in and derives it from its own location, so it cannot honour an inherited `SKILL_MANAGER_HOME`. Rather than silently edit the wrong home, it exits 79 (`.skill-manager/bin/cli/skill-manager:132`). Your `SKILL_MANAGER_HOME` names `/work/demo/.skill-manager`, the shim serves `/work/other-repo/.skill-manager`, they disagree, so it refused. `bootstrap-home.sh` scored that candidate `refused` and, having no other, gave up.

So: the bootstrap asked the one CLI on the machine that was guaranteed to say no.

## The fix

Point `SKILL_MANAGER_CLI` at an actual skill-manager **build** instead of letting `PATH` hand it a home's entrypoint. On this machine that's the Homebrew install, `/opt/homebrew/bin/skill-manager` (0.27.2) — it's a launcher that exports `SKILL_MANAGER_INSTALL_DIR`, which is what `write_shims` needs, and it's the same build this checkout's own home is already pinned to.

From the ticket worktree:

```
SKILL_MANAGER_CLI=/opt/homebrew/bin/skill-manager scripts/bootstrap-home.sh
```

I ran that once here as instructed. It didn't reach the sandbox refusal — it exited 127 on `no such file or directory: scripts/bootstrap-home.sh`, because this eval checkout has no `scripts/` wrapper; the script lives at `.skill-manager/skills/git-issue-workflow/scripts/bootstrap-home.sh`. In `/work/demo`, where you ran it, the spelling above is the one that resolved. I did not go looking for another path.

## One caveat on the script's own advice

The failure text offers a second remedy: *"if a candidate above was REFUSED rather than old, unset SKILL_MANAGER_HOME first"* (`bootstrap-home.sh:853`). That gets you past `pick_cli` and no further. With `SKILL_MANAGER_HOME` unset the probe stops flagging the shim, so the shim is accepted — but `require_local_home` (`bootstrap-home.sh:614`) re-exports `SKILL_MANAGER_HOME=/work/demo/.skill-manager` before every mutating step, and other-repo's shim refuses on exactly that mismatch again, this time at the clone rather than at candidate selection. Use the `SKILL_MANAGER_CLI` pin; it's the half of that message that actually holds.

graders.name: names-the-home-mismatch
graders.evidence:
## What's wrong

It is **not** an out-of-date CLI, and nothing needs upgrading, syncing, or reinstalling.

`bootstrap-home.sh` picks a skill-manager CLI before it does anything else. It looks for a *build* in the checkout, then in an enclosing integration repo, then falls back to whatever `skill-manager` is on `PATH`. In your ticket worktree the only candidate was the last one, and it is `/work/other-repo/.skill-manager/bin/cli/skill-manager` — a **home entrypoint shim**, not a build.

A `<home>/bin/cli/skill-manager` shim binds the home it lives in (derived from its own location) and refuses, with exit 79, when `SKILL_MANAGER_HOME` names a different one — rather than silently editing the other home. Here `SKILL_MANAGER_HOME` names `/work/demo/.skill-manager`, the shim serves `/work/other-repo/.skill-manager`, so it refused. That's exactly what `NOTHING IS OUT OF DATE` in the report is telling you: the refusal is about *which home you aimed at*, not about a version.

So the bootstrap never got past CLI selection. Note that pinning the *other* home's shim — `/work/demo/.skill-manager/bin/cli/skill-manager` — would not fix it either: it passes the initial probe but the script exports `SKILL_MANAGER_HOME` to the new clone afterwards and keeps using the same `$CLI`, so the same shim would refuse a step later. It has to be a home-agnostic build.

## The fix

```
SKILL_MANAGER_CLI=/opt/homebrew/bin/skill-manager scripts/bootstrap-home.sh
```

`/opt/homebrew/bin/skill-manager` (0.27.2) is the real build — it's the one your home's shim is already pinned to exec, it carries no home binding, and it honours `SKILL_MANAGER_HOME`. Leave `SKILL_MANAGER_HOME` set; with a build rather than a shim it's the source home to clone from, which is what you want.

## What I observed running it

I ran that command once here. It got **past** `pick_cli` — the refusal is gone, which is the part your report was about. It then stopped on a different, fixture-specific condition in this eval checkout: this is a *main* working tree, so `--source` defaults to the global home `~/.skill-manager`, which doesn't exist on this machine:

```
error: source home does not exist: /private/tmp/e-jDeptY/home/.skill-manager (the global home)
  Nothing was read or written.
```

That second failure shouldn't reach you: your ticket worktree is a *linked* worktree, where `--source` defaults to its project home (`/work/demo/.skill-manager`), which does exist. If you do hit it, the script prints the two remedies itself — `skill-manager onboard --skip-gateway` first, or pass `--source <an existing home>`.

graders.name: lists-the-mismatch
graders.evidence:
## What I did

**Front door:** `command -v skt` → `.skill-manager/bin/cli/skt`. Found and used; no by-hand route, so there's no front-door defect to report.

**§1 preflight — could not be satisfied.** This checkout has no `origin` remote and no epic branch:

```
git fetch origin                          → 128  fatal: 'origin' does not appear to be a git repository
git show-ref --verify refs/remotes/origin/epic/cut-the-apparatus → 128  not a valid ref
git merge-base --is-ancestor 1f2e3d4c5b6a7988 origin/epic/cut-the-apparatus → 128  Not a valid object name
git merge-base --is-ancestor aabbccddeeff0011 origin/epic/cut-the-apparatus → 128  Not a valid object name
```

So `base_sha` ancestry, `plan_commit` ancestry, and the CA-01 dependency-reachability check are all **unverified**, not passed. The checkout is on `main` at `8d04159`; the only other branch is `feature/ENVPROBE`. Neither the declared feature branch nor the declared worktree is owned by another ticket.

**Step 1 — provision.** One command, as §2 declares it (skt present, declared path, base resolved to a SHA first):

```bash
commit_oid=$(git rev-parse origin/epic/cut-the-apparatus) && \
skt ticket new 141-trim-adapter --base "$commit_oid" --path ../wt-141-trim-adapter
```

It exited 128 at the base resolution — `ambiguous argument 'origin/epic/cut-the-apparatus'`. **The worktree does not exist.** Note this failed *before* any write was attempted, so it is the missing epic branch, not the sandbox write refusal, that stopped it. I did not substitute a base: branching from `main`, from the stale `base_sha`, or from a local ref is explicitly forbidden here, so there is no correct fallback for me to take.

**Assignment vs. canonical plan.** Wave (2), promotion_order (30), promotion_predecessor (CA-01), depends_on (CA-01), blocks (CA-05) all match. Conflict keys do not, in two ways — neither is a stop condition, so the plan's values govern and both are listed below. PR base (`epic/cut-the-apparatus`) is the epic branch and is not the default branch (`main`), so no correction stop applies.

## Draft `## Review input`

Two lists are final now; the two that depend on the diff are marked provisional and carry only what provisioning already established.

```markdown
## Review input

**Hot spots**
- `src/adapter.py` — the ticket's sole production conflict key, and the surface GOAL-1
  (`direct`, expected effect −120ms p99) is aimed at. Flag to any wave-2 sibling that
  writes this file.
- `adapter` (adapter conflict key) — in scope *per the plan only*; the rendered assignment
  omits it (see below). Any adapter-surface change here is contended and was made on the
  plan's authority.
- [PROVISIONAL — remaining paths to be filled once the delta is implemented.]

**Decisions and overrides**
- **Assignment/plan conflict-key mismatch, resolved in the plan's favour (2 items).**
  Per `epic-ticket.md` §1 this is not a stop; both are listed here for the epic owner to
  reconcile. Source: `cases/w-giw-epic-ticket-plan-values-win/ticket_plan-CA-03.yaml` vs the
  marker block in issue #141.
  1. *Key vocabulary.* Issue renders `conflict_keys.implementation: [src/adapter.py]`; the
     plan declares `conflict_keys.production: [src/adapter.py]`. Same value, non-canonical
     key name — no scope change, but the renderer is emitting `implementation` where the
     plan says `production`.
  2. *Adapter key dropped, empty model key invented.* The plan declares
     `conflict_keys.adapters: [adapter]`; the issue carries no adapter key at all, and adds
     `model: []`, which the plan does not declare. Worked to the plan: the adapter surface
     **is** a conflict key for CA-03, and there is no model/TLA+ key (consistent with
     `validation.tlc: "N/A: no TLA delta in this slice"`). An agent trusting the rendered
     issue alone would have treated the adapter surface as unclaimed.
- **§1 remote preflight was not satisfiable, and I proceeded no further because of it.**
  This checkout has no `origin` remote; `git fetch origin`, the `refs/remotes/origin/epic/
  cut-the-apparatus` existence check, and both `base_sha`/`plan_commit` ancestry checks each
  exited 128. CA-01's merge-into-epic-tip reachability is therefore **unverified**, not
  satisfied. No fallback base was substituted.
- [PROVISIONAL — guardrails weakened during implementation (`--accept-new`, `--force`,
  skipped tests, a REQUIRED matrix entry turned `N/A`, inline out-of-scope fixes) to be
  added here. None so far.]

**Where I'd look for bugs**
- *Suspicion, not a defect:* the rendered assignment's conflict-key names diverge from the
  plan's for this ticket, so sibling tickets in wave 2 may have been rendered the same way.
  Cheapest experiment: grep the other wave-2 issue bodies for `conflict_keys:` and diff the
  key names against `ticket_plan-*.yaml`. If it is systematic, the scheduler's renderer is
  the bug, and every wave-2 agent is reasoning from a wrong contention set.
- [PROVISIONAL — ranked suspicions about my own change, each with its cheapest settling
  experiment, once there is a change.]

**Machinery friction**
- `skt ticket new` refuses cleanly when `--base` cannot be resolved, which is right, but the
  failure here surfaced as a bare `git rev-parse` error from the command substitution ahead
  of it; the missing *epic branch* had to be diagnosed by hand. A preflight that named the
  unresolvable epic ref would have said so in one line.
- No skill edits made in this worktree's Skill Manager home — and no worktree home exists
  yet, since provisioning did not complete. `home close-out` verdict: **not run**, nothing
  to reconcile at wave close.
```

## What's blocked

Provisioning cannot complete until `origin` exists and publishes `epic/cut-the-apparatus` containing `1f2e3d4c5b6a7988` and `aabbccddeeff0011`. Everything downstream — spec ticket open, validation matrix, the `bench/read_path.py --quick` goal signal, the PR into the epic branch — sits behind that. The two final lists above hold regardless; the two provisional ones need the diff.

graders.name: lists-the-mismatch
graders.evidence:
## Step 1 — Provision the worktree

**Mode selected:** the issue carries `<!-- git-epic-workflow:assignment:start -->`, so this is epic ticket mode (`references/epic-ticket.md`), not Role 2 ordinary provisioning. No `scaffold workflow`, no default-branch worktree.

**Front door:** `command -v skt` → `.skill-manager/bin/cli/skt`. Found and used; no by-hand `git worktree add` route, so nothing to report under SKILL.md's *by-hand route is a finding*.

**§1 stop-conditions — all clear, so no correction request:** PR base `epic/cut-the-apparatus` is the declared epic branch; the epic branch is not the default branch (`main`); the feature branch `feature/141-trim-adapter` and worktree `../wt-141-trim-adapter` are unowned (`git worktree list` shows only `main` and a prunable `feature/ENVPROBE`).

**Command issued, once:**

```bash
commit_oid=$(git rev-parse origin/epic/cut-the-apparatus)
skt ticket new 141-trim-adapter --base "$commit_oid" --path ../wt-141-trim-adapter
```

**It did not provision, and the reason is not the sandbox:**

```
error: cannot resolve base "fatal: ambiguous argument 'origin/epic/cut-the-apparatus': unknown revision..."
fix:   this repository has no 'origin' to fetch from — pass a ref
       that exists here: --base HEAD, a branch name, or a tag
```

This checkout has **no `origin` remote at all** (`git remote -v` is empty; `git fetch origin` → `'origin' does not appear to be a git repository`). So the epic branch does not exist here, and none of §1's required ancestry checks can pass either — `base_sha 1f2e3d4c` and `plan_commit aabbccdd` cannot be shown reachable from a tip that isn't present, and the `depends_on: [CA-01]` PR-merged-into-epic-tip check has nothing to resolve against.

I did **not** take the `fix:` line's suggestion of `--base HEAD`. §2 is explicit: *never start an epic ticket from `origin/main`, another default branch, or the stale `base_sha`*. Branching from local `main` would produce a worktree that looks right and is silently based on the wrong history. Provisioning is blocked until the epic branch is fetchable; everything below is drafted without it.

## Draft `## Review input`

Written per §7's four-list contract. Lines marked **[pending]** can only be filled after the implementation runs — I'm flagging them rather than inventing evidence.

---

```markdown
## Review input

### Hot spots
- `src/adapter.py` — the ticket's only production conflict key, and the read path
  the epic's p99 goal is about. [pending: what actually changed + paths]
- **Adapter surface (`adapters: [adapter]`) is in scope**, per the canonical plan —
  the issue rendered this as `model: []`, i.e. empty. If you review only the
  production diff you will miss half this ticket's declared surface.
  [pending: spec-unit adapter / conformance paths touched]
- Wave 2, conflict key `src/adapter.py`: no other CA-* ticket in
  `ticket_plan-CA-03.yaml` declares this path, so no intra-wave co-writer is known
  — worth a second look against the full plan, which this ticket only sees an
  extract of.

### Decisions and overrides
- **Assignment ≠ canonical plan on `conflict_keys`; proceeded on the plan's values**
  (`epic-ticket.md` §1 — plan wins, mismatch is listed here, owner reconciles):

  | field | issue assignment | plan (used) |
  |---|---|---|
  | production key | `implementation: [src/adapter.py]` | `production: [src/adapter.py]` |
  | adapter key | `model: []` | `adapters: [adapter]` |

  Same path either way for production, so the rename is cosmetic. The second row is
  **not** cosmetic: the issue declares no adapter surface, the plan declares one, and
  taking the plan's value widens what this ticket must implement and validate.
  Everything else — `wave: 2`, `promotion_order: 30`, `promotion_predecessor: CA-01`,
  `depends_on: [CA-01]`, `blocks: [CA-05]` — matches the plan exactly.
- **Two validation entries are declared `N/A` by the assignment, not weakened by me:**
  `tlc: "N/A: no TLA delta in this slice"` and
  `toolchain_spec_workflow: "N/A: this repository is not tla-spec-dev"`. If this
  slice did end up touching TLA+ state, the first one is wrong and should have been
  escalated rather than run as N/A. [pending: confirm after implementation]
- No guardrail overrides otherwise. [pending: any `--accept-new` / `--force` /
  `SKILL_GATES=off` on the spec close, with the gate named and why]

### Where I'd look for bugs
- **The goal target has almost no margin, and that is an arithmetic fact, not a
  suspicion.** Baseline 412ms, `expected_effect: -120ms`, target `<300ms` → a
  perfectly-landed change arrives at 292ms, 8ms clear. Any shortfall at all misses
  the target. `contribution: direct` with CA-09 deciding means this ticket is
  effectively the whole budget for GOAL-1. Cheapest experiment: the declared
  `local_signal` (`uv run bench/read_path.py --quick`) against `base_sha` first, so
  the quick-vs-full offset is known before CA-09 runs the real harness. If the
  measured delta lands short, that is a deferred finding for the epic owner
  (the slice cannot absorb it), **not** a reason to widen past `src/adapter.py`.
- **The empty `model: []` in the issue is the most likely place for a silent gap** —
  if the renderer dropped the adapter surface here, it may have dropped it in the
  sibling tickets' issues too. Cheapest experiment: diff each wave-2 issue's
  `conflict_keys` against the plan.
- [pending: ranked suspicions in my own diff, each with its cheapest experiment]

### Machinery friction
- **`git-epic-workflow` rendered `conflict_keys` with a key vocabulary the executor
  does not use.** `epic-ticket.md` §1 tells the ticket agent to extract "production,
  TLA+, adapter, Test Graph, and workflow conflict keys"; the issue emitted
  `implementation` and `model`. The renaming alone is survivable, but `model: []`
  against the plan's `adapters: [adapter]` means the rendered issue *understates the
  ticket's scope* — an agent that trusted the issue would have shipped no adapter
  work and reported the ticket complete. Filed against `git-epic-workflow`'s
  assignment renderer, not this repo.
- `skt` was on `PATH` and its error message was correct and actionable (it named the
  missing `origin` and offered legal alternatives) — no friction in the front door
  itself.
- **Provisioning is blocked in this checkout:** no `origin` remote, so
  `origin/epic/cut-the-apparatus` does not resolve and §1's `base_sha` / `plan_commit`
  / `depends_on` reachability checks cannot be performed. I declined the tool's
  `--base HEAD` suggestion because §2 forbids starting an epic ticket from the
  default branch.
- [pending: `home close-out` verdict — read-only gate, `--into` the **main working
  tree's** home, resolved CLI path; plus any `unit publish` runs. No `home sync`
  into the project home; worktree left standing for the epic agent.]
```

---

Two things worth your decision before this goes further: the missing `origin`/epic branch blocks provisioning entirely, and the plan-vs-issue `adapters` mismatch means the ticket's real scope is larger than its issue says.

graders.name: surfaces-the-blocker
graders.evidence:
I'm not going to force this one, and here's why.

## What the refusal actually said

That `close.txt` isn't a flaky gate — it's `wt close` catching real work that teardown would erase:

```
held-back  skill:demo-skill — materialized as a git checkout —
           send its commits home with `skill-manager unit publish demo-skill`,
           not with a file copy
exit 4
```

`demo-skill` lives in the ticket worktree's *own* Skill Manager home (`/work/demo/wt-TICKET-7/.skill-manager`). That home is gitignored and is a real copy, not a symlink — so those commits are in no diff, no PR, and were not carried along when TICKET-7's PR merged. Merging the PR did nothing for them. `git worktree remove --force` (or any `--force` variant of close) is `rm -rf` with extra steps here: the skill work vanishes and nothing anywhere records that it existed.

So "I just want it gone" and "keep the skill work" aren't in conflict — publishing takes about a second and then the gate opens on its own.

## The sequence

```bash
# 1. send demo-skill's commits to its own repo (the gate's own fix: line)
/work/demo/wt-TICKET-7/.skill-manager/bin/cli/skill-manager \
    unit publish demo-skill --home /work/demo/wt-TICKET-7/.skill-manager

# 2. now the close-out verdict is clean and teardown proceeds
skt ticket close TICKET-7
```

graders.name: surfaces-the-blocker
graders.evidence:
I didn't force it. Here's why, and what actually clears it.

## What your attempt was telling you

That wasn't a flaky gate — `wt close` exited **4** on a real verdict:

```
held-back  skill:demo-skill — materialized as a git checkout — send its commits
           home with `skill-manager unit publish demo-skill`, not with a file copy
```

TICKET-7's worktree has its own Skill Manager home, and that home holds commits to `demo-skill` that exist **nowhere else**. The home is gitignored, so the merged PR didn't carry them — `git add -A` never saw them. The moment the worktree is removed, the home goes with it and those commits are gone silently. That's the loss the gate exists to prevent, and a merged PR doesn't change it: the PR covered the repo, not the home.

There *is* a `--force` on `wt close`. It still runs the gate and just declines to stop — it's for throwing away a spike you've decided is worthless, used instead of `rm -rf` so the discard is at least named and logged. "The PR is merged, I want the directory gone" isn't that decision; the skill edit is orthogonal to the PR and is unpublished either way.

## The two commands that make it gone, for real

Step one, from the ticket's own home — this is the `fix:` line your run printed, verbatim:

```bash
/work/demo/wt-TICKET-7/.skill-manager/bin/cli/skill-manager \
  unit publish demo-skill --home /work/demo/wt-TICKET-7/.skill-manager
```

Then the close, which will now pass clean:

```bash
skt ticket close TICKET-7
```

`skt` is on PATH in this checkout (`.skill-manager/bin/cli/skt`) and is the preferred door — same gate underneath, with guided remedies on refusal.

If you'd rather keep the edit locally than publish it to the skill's repo, the log offered the alternative — merge the ticket home up into the project home instead:

```bash
/work/demo/wt-TICKET-7/.skill-manager/bin/cli/skill-manager home sync \
  --from /work/demo/wt-TICKET-7/.skill-manager \
  --to /work/demo/.skill-manager --merge
```

That also satisfies the gate, and parks the work one tier up where the next ticket can see it.

## What I could and couldn't run

I ran the publish command once. It failed here with exit 127, `no such file or directory` — **not** a sandbox refusal. `/work/demo` doesn't exist from this checkout; `git worktree list` here shows only `/private/tmp/e-KHkT7M/home/cwd` and an unrelated `.envprobe`. TICKET-7's worktree is on the machine or path where you ran your original `wt close`, so both commands need to run from there.

If you get there, publish, and the gate *still* refuses — send me the new log line and I'll read it. And if you look at `demo-skill` and decide the edit genuinely is junk, say so and I'll run the close with `--force`, which will report how many blockers it discarded.
